gloss: inevitably; willy-nilly; like it or not

definitions.gloss: inevitably; willy-nilly; whether one likes it or not
definitions.explanation: Describes something that happens regardless of one's wishes or consent. Indicates that there is no choice in the matter—it will happen whether you want it to or not.

examples.japanese: {否応|いやおう}なく{決断|けつだん}を{迫|せま}られた。
examples.english: I was forced to make a decision whether I liked it or not.

examples.japanese: グローバル{化|か}で{否応|いやおう}なく{英語|えいご}が{必要|ひつよう}になった。
examples.english: With globalization, English became inevitably necessary.

examples.japanese: {時代|じだい}の{流|なが}れに{否応|いやおう}なく{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる。
examples.english: One gets swept up in the currents of the times, like it or not.

notes:
FORMATION:
{否|いや} (no, unwilling) + {応|おう} (yes, consent) + なく (without)
Literally: "without yes or no" → regardless of one's wishes

VARIANTS:
・{否応|いやおう}なしに - Same meaning
・{否応|いやおう}なく - Standard form
・{有無|うむ}を{言|い}わさず - Without allowing objection (similar nuance)

USAGE:
{否応|いやおう}なく typically precedes verbs describing being forced into a situation or having to accept something:
・{否応|いやおう}なく{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる (to be inevitably drawn in)
・{否応|いやおう}なく{従|したが}う (to comply whether one likes it or not)
・{否応|いやおう}なく{変|か}わる (to change inevitably)

NUANCE:
Emphasizes the lack of choice—external circumstances or forces leave no room for refusal. Often used for societal changes, obligations, or situations beyond one's control.
